sentences.text:
THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 07.11.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2024:KER:82908 BAIL APPL. NO. 8729 OF 2024  2  Dated this the 7th day of November, 2024  ORDER
The application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for an order of pre-arrest bail.

2. The petitioners are the accused 1 to 4 in Crime No.1062/2024 of the Nedumbassery Airport Police Station, Ernakulam, which is registered against them for allegedly committing the offence punishable under Section 498A r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The prosecution case, in brief, is that: the first accused was married to the de facto complainant on 31.10.2010.

The accused 2 to 4 are the sister, brother and mother of the first accused,
respectively.

During the period of the cohabitation of the de facto complainant with the accused persons, between May 2014 and 8.6.2024, the accused mentally and physically 2024:KER:82908 BAIL APPL. NO. 8729 OF 2024 harassed the de facto complainant demanding more dowry.

Thus,
the accused have committed the above offence.

4. Heard; Sri.Thomas J.Anakkallunkal, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Sri.
C.S. Hrithwik., the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are totally innocent of the accusations levelled against them.
The fact that the marriage between the couple took place on 31.10.2010, but Annexure A1 FIR is registered only on 5.10.2024, proves the falsity and frivolity in the crime.
The marital relationship between the first petitioner and the de facto complainant is strained.
It is only to pressurise the petitioners to yield to the de facto complainant's unlawful demands, that she has registered Annexure A1 FIR.
The petitioners are law-abiding citizens without any criminal antecedents.
The petitioners' custodial interrogation is not necessary.
The petitioners are 2024:KER:82908 BAIL APPL. NO. 8729 OF 2024 ready to abide by any stringent condition that may be imposed by this Court and also co-operate with the investigation.
Hence, the application may be allowed.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the application.
He submitted that the investigation is in progress.
He also stated that if the petitioners are granted an order of pre-arrest bail, it may hamper the investigation.
Hence, the application may be dismissed.

sentences.text: The prosecution case is that, the petitioners who are the husband and in-laws of the de facto complainant had mentally and physically harassed her during the period from the year 2014 to 8.6.2024.
Indisputably, Annexure A1 FIR is registered only on 5.10.2024.
Prima facie, there is no plausible explanation for the delay.
Apparently, there also seems to be a marital discord between the couple.
However, these are matters to be investigated and ultimately decided after trial.

In Bhadres Bipinbhai Sheth vs State of Gujarat and another [2015 KHC 4579], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has succinctly culled out the principles for the purpose of grant of an order of pre-arrest bail in offences of a similar nature, by holding that the complaint made against the accused has to be thoroughly examined at the stage of considering a bail application, especially to find out if it is a false or frivolous complaint.

entities.text: Bhadres Bipinbhai Sheth vs State of Gujarat and another [2015 KHC 4579]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The courts should examine whether there is any family dispute between the parties and whether the Investigating Officer is acting in connivance with the complainant.
The gravity of each charge and the exact role of the accused should also be properly comprehended.

The discretion to grant an order of pre-arrest bail must be exercised on the basis of the available materials and the facts of the particular case and there is no requirement that the accused must make out a special case to exercise the power of grant of anticipatory bail.

The discretion of the Court should 2024:KER:82908 BAIL APPL. NO. 8729 OF 2024 be exercised with due care and circumspection, and the frivolity in the prosecution should be examined, particularly whether any harassment, humiliation or unjustified detention of the accused.

9. After bestowing my anxious consideration to the facts, the materials placed on record, and the rival submissions made across the Bar, and taking note of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the afore-cited decision, and on considering the fact that the marital relationship between the first petitioner and the de facto complainant is strained, and further that there is a delay in registering Annexure A1 FIR, I am satisfied and convinced that the petitioners had made out valid grounds to invoke the discretionary jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the BNS.
Hence, I am inclined to allow the application, but subject to stringent conditions.
(iii) The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer between 9 a.m and 11 a.m for two days from the date of their release.
